2026-09-16 (verify-text-coverage.mjs widening pass, `review` reset from 'human' back to 'ai' — real annotation-span change below): `moveSearchLibraryOrGraveyard-effect-structural.ts`'s own per-zone annotations (previously the bare noun "your library"/"graveyard" alone) now span the WHOLE "search your library and/or graveyard for an artifact card with mana value 2 or less, reveal it, and put it into your hand" clause for all 4 facts (2 source, 2 sink) — closes a real, substantial verify-text-coverage.mjs gap (this card was the ONLY real pool card using this recognizer, confirmed before widening). The trailing "If you search your library this way, shuffle." sentence is now a real `annotatedNonFactSpans` entry (kind: 'definition-path' — maps to this same Effect's own real `shuffleAfter: true` field, per this file's own pre-existing knownGaps note below documenting there's no separate Fact vocabulary for a bare shuffle consequence). verify-synergy.mjs/vitest/tsc all re-run clean. `npx tsx functional-model/scripts/verify-text-coverage.mjs --threshold=1.0 delivery-moogle` now reports 100%.

Migrated to the current unified Fact/annotations model (2026-09-11, continuation of the fin/1-10 rollout). Real oracle text (Scryfall-verified, fin/15): 'Flying / When this creature enters, search your library and/or graveyard for an artifact card with mana value 2 or less, reveal it, and put it into your hand. If you search your library this way, shuffle.' {3}{W}, Creature — Moogle, 3/2. Two baseline facts every card in this rollout gets: `self-cast` ({event:'cast', from:'Hand', target:'self'}, typeLine-anchored 'Creature') and `self-enters` ({event:'entersBattlefield', to:'Battlefield', controller:'you', subject:'self', target:'self'}, typeLine-anchored 'Creature'). The real ability is a genuine 'and/or' choice between TWO distinct origins (Library, Graveyard), authored as TWO separate SOURCE facts rather than one ambiguous-origin fact, since the oracle text names both zones explicitly: `{to:'Hand', from:'Library', controller:'you', types:{has:['Artifact']}, cmc:{max:2}}` (renders as 'tutor', the existing shared Library->Hand label) and `{to:'Hand', from:'Graveyard', controller:'you', types:{has:['Artifact']}, cmc:{max:2}}` (renders as a BRAND NEW 'regrowth' label — `ZONE_MOVEMENT_NAMES` had no Graveyard->Hand entry before this card; named after the classic reprinted sorcery Regrowth, same 'borrow the short common MTG term for the effect archetype' convention `tutor`/Demonic Tutor already established; deliberately NOT reusing card.ts's own existing `graveyard-recursion` tag, which names a different concept — casting FROM the graveyard via an alternate cost, not returning a card TO hand). Both source facts carry the real `cmc:{max:2}` constraint (this card is textually MORE precise than Cloud's/Ashe's own tutors, which have no mv restriction) — confirmed currently INERT for matching (factsInteract's zone-zone branch only checks a SOURCE's own types/cmc against an UNCONSTRAINED want, which always short-circuits true before reading them; a CONSTRAINED want would need the matched producer's own `CardDefinition.cmc` populated to check against, and `cmc` is an opt-in-only static field almost nothing in the pool sets), same class of documented-but-inert constraint Ashe's own 'types:{has:[Artifact]} inert on a SOURCE fact' finding already established — not a bug, honest documentation of a real, pre-existing, pool-wide gap. Kept both pre-existing SINK facts (`wants-artifact-in-library`, `wants-artifact-in-graveyard`) migrated to the unified shape (`to` instead of `zone`, no `id`/`sourceText`/`highlight`, `annotations` computed) rather than removing them the way Ashe's own analogous 'wants-artifact-in-library' sink was removed — that removal was a specific, live, user-driven Facts-tab call for THAT card ('let's remove'), not a general rule; this rollout's own adelbert-steiner precedent explicitly KEEPS a real, correctly-shaped, 0-incoming-match sink as a normal, tolerated pool-authoring gap, so delivery-moogle's two sinks default to the same treatment absent a direct instruction to remove them. Added `cmc:{max:2}` to both sinks too, for the same textual-precision reason as the sources (real, measured tradeoff — see find-synergies.mjs diff below).

Engine/harness fixes made along the way (real bugs surfaced by writing this card's own scenario, fixed rather than routed around, per project convention): (1) `card.ts`'s own `CardDefinition.custom` effect on this card previously had a STALE, INCORRECT comment claiming mana value couldn't be filtered at all ('not tracked anywhere on Card/RealCard') and citing a nonexistent comment on cloud-midgar-mercenary as precedent (grepped that file — no such comment/restriction exists there, Cloud's own search has no mv gate at all). Checked interfaces.ts/state.ts/harness.ts fresh: `Card.getCMC()` is real (interfaces.ts ~line106, citing Card.java ~line7227), backed by a real `RealCard.getCMC` (state.ts) and already wired into `harness.ts`'s `loggingCard` wrap (`read:getCMC` trace evidence). Fixed the effect for real: `run()` now filters `c.isArtifact() && c.getCMC() <= 2`, matching the real oracle text precisely, with real `read:getCMC` trace evidence in both scenarios below (not just documented as a gap). (2) Added `harness.ts` `PlayerState.graveyardArtifactCount` (mirrors the pre-existing `libraryArtifactCount`) — the graveyard search branch was previously real, executable code with literally zero way to seed a real graveyard artifact candidate via any scenario; this was a real, fixable harness gap (a missing setup field), not a permanent engine limitation, so it's fixed rather than left as an untestable claim. (3) Converted `scenarios.ts` from the old flat `trigger:'onEnter'`-only shape (which never exercises cast/enters lifecycle at all, so the two baseline facts had ZERO real trace evidence and verify-synergy correctly hard-failed on first pass) to a real engine-piloted `runEngineScenarios()` (added `on:'enter'` to the trigger in definition.ts for real 603.6b auto-fire), same convention Cloud/Ashe already use — TWO separate real playthroughs (Library-branch, Graveyard-branch with library artifact count 0 so the real 'and/or' pool structurally falls through to Graveyard). (4) Real bug found (and fixed for THIS card, flagged not fixed for the rest of the pool) while building those playthroughs: an `EnginePilotSetup` with no `opponents` produces a genuinely 1-player GameState; `turn.ts`'s `shouldSkipDraw` correctly requires `playerCount===2` for CR103.8a's specifically-2-player 'skip the first draw' rule, so a 1-player pilot does NOT skip its opening draw, silently drawing the seeded library artifact into hand during `setupEnginePilot` itself, before the card's own ETB ever runs (confirmed via a scratch debug script: the artifact was already in `you.hand` before `pilotCast` was even called). Fixed by giving both of this card's own playthroughs a real second player (`opponents: [{basicLands:['Forest'], libraryCount:5}]`, same shape Ashe's own scenario already uses) — see scenarios.ts's own extensive comment for the full writeup, including the SAME bug independently reproduced live against cloud-midgar-mercenary's own checked-in scenario (its seeded library artifact is ALSO drawn away before its own pilotCast, and its real ETB then runs against an artifact-less library and finds nothing) PLUS a second, independent bug this card's own `custom` effect never triggers: `harness.ts`'s shared declarative `move` action (`move: (player, from, to, qty, validType) => {...}`) logs `fn:'move'` UNCONDITIONALLY even when its own `chosen` array is empty, so Cloud's checked-in trace.json's apparent 'successful tutor' line is fabricated by the log, not real — this card's own `custom` effect can't hit this because it already guards `if (pool.length===0) return;` before calling `moveTo`. NEITHER of these two shared-plumbing bugs was fixed pool-wide in this task (flagged to the parent session/engine notes instead) — fixing the shared `move` helper could flip other currently-'passing' cards' verify-synergy evidence checks and needs its own full-pool audit, out of scope for a single-card migration.

Real find-synergies.mjs diff (isolated: reverted just this card's synergy.json to git HEAD, re-ran the full pool, diffed lines mentioning 'Delivery Moogle', restored): 17 -> 132 lines. LOST (all 17 old lines): old presence-shaped 'graveyard presence'/'hand presence' matches — the 2 hand-presence ones (Nibelheim Aflame, The Water Crystal) are NOT gone, just relabeled ('tutor'/'regrowth', 2 lines each, +2 net from the new regrowth fact); the 15 real graveyard-presence ones ARE genuinely gone: 13 are real cmc>2 artifacts (Diamond Weapon cmc9, Omega cmc7, Aettir and Priwen cmc6, four Legendary Artifacts at cmc4, The Prima Vista cmc5, etc. — checked every one against data/fin/fin_scryfall.json) sitting in a pre-migration card's own bare presence-shaped SOURCE fact, which the OLD unconstrained sink used to accept indiscriminately (a real overclaim — Delivery Moogle's own ability could never actually find a cmc9 Diamond Weapon) and the new `cmc:{max:2}`-gated sink correctly rejects; 2 (Excalibur II cmc1, Lunatic Pandora cmc1) are REAL cmc-eligible cards that SHOULD still match but can't, purely because `CardDefinition.cmc` is an opt-in-only static field neither of those two cards' own definition.ts populates (staticAttrsFor resolves `cmc: undefined`, satisfiesNum(undefined, {max:2}) is false regardless of the real printed cost) — a pre-existing, pool-wide authoring gap, not something this card's own migration can fix. GAINED: 128 real 'enters the battlefield' matches via the new baseline `self-enters` fact (pure gain, the card had no such baseline before), 2 'tutor' + 2 'regrowth' matches (Nibelheim Aflame, The Water Crystal — both real, already-established unconstrained hand-presence wants, same 2 cards Ashe's/Cloud's own identical-shaped facts already match). Net card-level count: 132 lines, but the true signal is 'went from 2 old real tutor matches + 15 false-positive graveyard-cost overclaims to 4 real tutor/regrowth matches (same 2 cards, both directions) + 128 new baseline battlefield-presence matches, losing 2 real cmc-eligible matches only to an unrelated pool-wide gap'. `verify-synergy.mjs` (scoped delivery-moogle AND full pool): 0 hard failures either way (only expected soft `tapForMana`-unrecognized-action notes, same class every engine-piloted card's own casting scaffolding gets). `npx vitest run functional-model`: 238/238. `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
knownGaps: Neither seeded filler artifact (library or graveyard) is given an explicit cmc in its own scenario (defaults to RealCard.cmc ?? 0), so no scenario here proves the mv-2-or-less filter actually EXCLUDES a real >2-mv candidate — both real scenarios only demonstrate it correctly ADMITTING a 0-mv one. A future scenario proving the negative case would need a libraryArtifactCmc/graveyardArtifactCmc-style harness field this task didn't add.

The card's own `cmc:{max:2}` constraint (source AND sink) is textually correct but presently INERT for real matching in most cases: factsInteract never checks a SOURCE's own types/cmc against an UNCONSTRAINED want (always short-circuits true), and a CONSTRAINED want needs the matched producer's own CardDefinition.cmc populated, which almost nothing in the pool sets (opt-in-only field). Same class as Ashe's own documented 'types on a SOURCE fact is inert' gap.

'If you search your library this way, shuffle' is a real, specific mechanical consequence of the real oracle text, deliberately not modeled as a separate fact (state.ts's own header rules out anything beyond the action vocabulary this model actually uses; no downstream fact/consumer reads a library-shuffle state anywhere in the pool).

Two real, distinct shared-plumbing bugs found while building this card's own scenarios, NOT fixed pool-wide (flagged to engine notes / parent session instead): (1) an EnginePilotSetup with no `opponents` produces a genuinely 1-player game, where turn.ts's shouldSkipDraw correctly does NOT apply CR103.8a's 2-player-only 'skip first draw' rule — silently drawing away a seeded library/graveyard candidate before a card's own ETB runs; reproduced live against cloud-midgar-mercenary's own checked-in scenario, not just theorized. (2) harness.ts's shared declarative `move` action logs `fn:'move'` unconditionally even when its own `chosen` array is empty, so a scenario hit by bug (1) can still show a fabricated 'successful' move in its trace log — confirmed this makes cloud-midgar-mercenary's own checked-in trace.json's apparent tutor success line untrue today. This card's own `custom` effect is immune to bug (2) (it already guards on `pool.length===0` before calling `moveTo`), but was still fixed for bug (1) (added a real second player to its own scenarios) since that part was cheap and directly affected this card's own trace correctness.

Flying
When this creature enters, search your library and/or graveyard for an artifact card with mana value 2 or less, reveal it, and put it into your hand. If you search your library this way, shuffle.

If you search your library this way, shuffle." — maps to this card's own real `Effect.shuffleAfter: true` field (definition.ts), a real, mechanically-enforced CR 701.19 consequence, but has no Fact of its own — no vocabulary exists anywhere in this pool for a bare 'then shuffle' consequence (see this file's own pre-existing knownGaps entry documenting the same conclusion, predating this formalization).
